# Assumptions — Team Chat Application

**Artifact:** Assumptions
**Stage:** 1 of 7 (Exercise 2)
**Status:** Draft (generated by Claude Opus — Step 1: Generate)
**Source ask:** *"We need a chat application so that our team members can chat with one another."*

---

## Purpose

This document captures the assumptions we are making about the chat application,
its users, its scope, and its constraints. Because the original ask is a single
sentence with no detailed requirements, every downstream artifact (requirements,
specifications, test cases, architecture, and code) depends on the assumptions
recorded here. These assumptions are explicit so they can be challenged, validated,
and refined.

Each assumption has a unique ID (`A-NN`), a statement, a rationale, and a
confidence level (High / Medium / Low). Low-confidence assumptions are the ones
most in need of validation with the requesting leader.

---

## 1. Business & Context Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Rationale | Confidence |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| A-01 | The application is for **internal team communication** within a single organization, not a public-facing product. | The ask says "our team members." | High |
| A-02 | The primary goal is **real-time text conversation** among colleagues. | "chat with one another" implies live messaging. | High |
| A-03 | The expected user base is **small to medium** (roughly 5–200 users) for the initial release. | "team" implies a bounded group, not enterprise-wide scale. | Medium |
| A-04 | The application must be delivered **quickly** as a working first version (MVP), with refinement to follow. | The compressed timeframe and vague ask favor an MVP. | High |
| A-05 | There is **no existing chat system** to integrate with or migrate from. | No starter code or integration was mentioned. | Medium |
| A-06 | Cost should be **modest**; the solution targets low-cost Azure tiers. | Internal tool, small team, MVP scope. | Medium |

## 2. User & Persona Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Rationale | Confidence |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| A-07 | All users are **trusted internal team members** (employees/contractors). | "our team members." | High |
| A-08 | Users access the app from a **modern web browser** on desktop and mobile. | A web app maximizes reach without installs; widest compatibility. | Medium |
| A-09 | Users need a **display name/identity** so messages are attributable. | Chatting requires knowing who said what. | High |
| A-10 | Users are **not highly technical** and expect a simple, familiar chat UI. | General team members, not just engineers. | Medium |
| A-11 | Users may be **distributed across locations and time zones**. | Modern teams are often remote/hybrid. | Medium |

## 3. Functional Scope Assumptions (MVP)

| ID | Assumption | Rationale | Confidence |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| A-12 | The MVP supports a **shared group chat room** (one common channel) for all team members. | Simplest form of "chat with one another"; fastest to deliver. | Medium |
| A-13 | Messages are **plain text**; rich media, file uploads, and reactions are out of scope for the MVP. | Keeps scope minimal for the timeframe. | Medium |
| A-14 | Users can **see message history** for the current session/room. | Context is needed to follow a conversation. | Medium |
| A-15 | Messages display the **sender name and a timestamp**. | Standard chat expectation. | High |
| A-16 | **Multiple users chatting simultaneously** are delivered messages in near real time. | Core to a chat experience. | High |
| A-17 | Out of scope for MVP: private/direct messages, multiple channels, threads, search, presence/typing indicators, notifications, message editing/deletion, and admin moderation. | Explicitly bounding scope to fit the timeframe; candidates for later iterations. | Medium |

## 4. Technical & Platform Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Rationale | Confidence |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| A-18 | The backend is built with **C# and .NET 10**. | Stated dependency for the Capstone. | High |
| A-19 | Real-time delivery is implemented with **ASP.NET Core SignalR** (WebSockets with fallback). | Native .NET real-time framework; ideal for chat. | High |
| A-20 | The frontend is a **lightweight web client** (HTML/CSS/JS, optionally Razor/Blazor) served by the same app. | Single deployable unit simplifies hosting and the timeframe. | Medium |
| A-21 | The application is deployed to **Azure App Service**. | Stated dependency for the Capstone. | High |
| A-22 | The MVP may use **in-memory state** for messages/connections; a durable database is a later enhancement. | Fastest path to a working demo; acceptable for MVP. | Medium |
| A-23 | A **single App Service instance** is sufficient for the MVP (no need for a SignalR backplane / Azure SignalR Service yet). | Small user base; scale-out is a later concern. | Medium |
| A-24 | Deployment and provisioning are performed via **GitHub Copilot + Azure MCP / azd**. | Stated tooling for the Capstone. | High |

## 5. Non-Functional Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Rationale | Confidence |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| A-25 | **Latency:** messages should appear to other users within ~1 second under normal load. | "Real-time" expectation for chat. | Medium |
| A-26 | **Availability:** best-effort uptime is acceptable for the MVP (no formal SLA). | Internal tool, MVP. | Medium |
| A-27 | **Security:** traffic is served over **HTTPS**; the app is reachable only by the intended audience. | Baseline expectation for any web app. | High |
| A-28 | **Authentication** beyond entering a display name is **out of scope for the MVP**, but the design should not preclude adding it later (e.g., Microsoft Entra ID). | Minimizes MVP complexity while leaving a path forward. | Low |
| A-29 | **Privacy/Compliance:** no regulated/sensitive data (PII, PHI, financial) is expected in chat content for the MVP. | Internal casual team chat assumption. | Low |
| A-30 | **Accessibility:** the UI should follow basic accessibility practices (keyboard usable, sufficient contrast). | Inclusive baseline. | Medium |

## Open Questions (to validate with the leader)

These map to the lowest-confidence assumptions and would be the first questions
asked in a real engagement:

1. **(A-28/A-07)** Is any authentication required, or is entering a display name enough for the first version?
2. **(A-12/A-17)** Is one shared room sufficient, or are multiple channels / direct messages needed soon?
3. **(A-22/A-14)** Must messages **persist** across restarts and sessions, or is session-only history acceptable for the MVP?
4. **(A-29)** Will any sensitive or regulated information be shared in chats? (Affects security/compliance requirements.)
5. **(A-03/A-23)** What is the realistic peak concurrent user count? (Affects scale-out and Azure SignalR decisions.)
6. **(A-08)** Is a web app acceptable, or are native mobile/desktop clients expected?

---

## Summary of Scope Decisions (MVP)

**In scope:** a single shared, real-time, text-only group chat room; web client;
sender name + timestamp; session message history; built with C#/.NET 10 + SignalR;
deployed to Azure App Service over HTTPS.

**Out of scope (MVP):** authentication beyond a display name, direct/private
messages, multiple channels, threads, file/media sharing, search, presence/typing
indicators, push notifications, message edit/delete, moderation, and durable
persistence.
